extractions.value: The authors propose the term 'Stiff Hemisyndrome' as a junction between SLS and SPS. The patient had a history of cervical spondylotic myelopathy treated with surgical decompression, which the authors hypothesize may have created a spinal cord fragility predisposing to anti-GAD-induced stiffness.
extractions.quote: We report a case of right-sided SLS, which could be defined as 'Stiff Hemisyndrome', as a junction between SLS and SPS. ... a link between SLS and previous cervical myelopathy can be suspected. ... this rise an hypothesis about interactions between SLS and spinal cord injuries that could induce a fragility in which anti-GAD induce stiffness
